doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Lips Lower Level, Buster Bennett, Israel Crosby and Stuff Smith
summary: Ware works a four-piece with Little Sax Crowder opposite Buster Bennett and Israel Crosby, then two weeks with Stuff Smith.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Uh huh. But when you came back to Chicago, you worked with Stuff Smith?

Yeah, I worked with Stuff. But first, I worked back -- Buster was working at a place called Lips Lower Level, which turned out to be the Blue Note; one of the top nightclubs. But I came back to Chicago, and I'm working down there with a local guy, Innocent Smith and Little Ruth Crowder;
Little Sax Crowder had a four-piece group; a tenor, trumpet, bass and piano. And I'm working with them ...

No drums. But Buster Bennett had a 4-piece band opposite us; they played 30 minutes and we played 30 minutes at this club -- the Lips Lower Level -- and what knocked me out, some old friends of mine, a piano player, and Israel Crosby Robert Montgomery and Jimmy [Bowlin] -- and that was another education; playing opposite that young man. I say 'young man' but playing and hearing all those beautiful notes he was putting out. With Buster and our band -- we would come close, you know, exchanging ideas.

And then somebody around the corner told Stuff Smith he needed a bass player; he was going to a club out at North Side. And so I worked for Stuff for 2 weeks. Then after Stuff, the next name I worked with was Roy Eldridge and Sonny Stitt.
